title: b42 M-layer twin replicates on fresh seed 3: with adsorption drift M rim/core 3.69 (160/169 membrane-like), with chim=0 0.975 (0/169), and every other channel, the cell count and the division record are identical
summary: Ran the claimed world and its matched diffusion-only twin (world_chim0.py: chim 4 -> 0, all else equal) unchanged on fresh seed 3, 128^2, T=100000. World: M peaks in the rim band (rho 0.75), rim/core 3.69, rim/outside 19.6, 160/169 individuals membrane-like. Twin: M peaks in the core (rho 0.15), rim/core 0.975, 0/169 membrane-like. Both arms have 30 final cells, 11 persistent splits, generation 3, 0 merges, and the same radial profiles of S, K, L, wall and yield (radial.png of both), because M feeds back on nothing. The layer is made by the adsorption drift and is passive, as the finding states. I did not repeat the resolution continuation or the mbeta screens.

observations.B: world/seed3/radial.png: M rim/core 3.69, 160/169 membrane-like; twin_chim0/seed3/radial.png: M rim/core 0.975, peak in the core, 0/169; all other channels identical between the two

seeds_run.result: pass: world M layer 3.69 vs twin 0.975; both 11 persistent splits, gen 3, 30 cells

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. The resolution continuation (1.5x) and the mbeta gate screens were not repeated. The twin shows that the layer comes from the drift, and also that it does no work: cells, division and every other channel are unchanged without it.
